title: Callability Is Not Operability: Controlled Interface Interventions for LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.23628v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A tool call can be perfectly valid yet still leave an autonomous agent unable to determine what to do next. For example, if an external effect commits but its response is lost, committed and uncommitted states may become indistinguishable to the agent even though they require different continuation actions. We study this gap between callability and operability: whether a tool interface exposes the action-relevant state and semantics needed for an agent to continue safely under operational uncertainty. We operationalize tool operability through Agent-First Tooling (AFT), a set of interface mechanisms spanning selective capability discovery, execution lifecycle and recovery, explicit external-effect semantics, machine-readable results, and postcondition verification. translated_title: 可调用性不等于可操作性：针对LLM代理的受控接口干预
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.23628v1 公告类型：新 摘要：一个工具调用可能完全有效，但仍使自主代理无法确定下一步该做什么。例如，如果外部效果已提交但其响应丢失，即使已提交和未提交状态需要不同的后续操作，代理也可能无法区分它们。我们研究了可调用性与可操作性之间的差距：工具接口是否暴露了代理在操作不确定性下安全继续所需的与动作相关的状态和语义。我们通过代理优先工具化（AFT）来操作化工具可操作性，这是一套接口机制，涵盖选择性能力发现、执行生命周期和恢复、明确的外部效果语义、机器可读结果以及后置条件验证。我们引入了AFT-Bench，一个受控接口干预框架，它保持任务、后端、初始状态、注入故障、代理和语言模型固定，同时仅改变接口设计。
tldr: 该论文提出了代理优先工具化（AFT）框架和AFT-Bench基准，揭示了工具接口的可调用性与可操作性之间的关键差距，并通过受控接口干预来提升LLM代理在操作不确定性下的安全性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Agent-First Tooling (AFT) and AFT-Bench to address the gap between tool callability and operability, enhancing LLM agent safety under operational uncertainty through controlled interface interventions.
